standfirst: Brewing Fundamentals is our starting course: four modules from mill to glass. Taken in person with the Beer Crosswords book, it costs ₹1,999. Here is what you get and why the book earns its place next to the course.
sections: ₹1,999 buys the course and the book together

The bundle is two things. The first is Brewing Fundamentals, taught in person in Pune, Delhi, Gurugram or Bengaluru. The second is Beer Crosswords, our 134-page printable A4 book of puzzles with answers. Together they cost ₹1,999.

For a sense of scale, the live online version of Brewing Fundamentals is listed at ₹5,999 on its own. The in-person bundle is priced for people who would rather learn standing next to a brewer than in front of a screen.
Four modules take you from mill to glass

The course follows the same four-module syllabus as our Brewing Fundamentals course page:

  1. Grain to glass. The four ingredients and the brewhouse map from mill to package.
  2. Malt, water and the mash. Mash at 62 to 65 °C (144 to 149 °F) for a drier beer or 68 to 70 °C (154 to 158 °F) for more body, with mash pH at 5.2 to 5.6.
  3. Hops, boil and yeast. Why alpha acids need the boil to turn bitter and how ale and lager yeast differ.
  4. Sanitation, kit and your first recipe. Cleaning versus sanitising, gravity readings and ABV = (OG - FG) x 131.25.

By the end you should be able to build a 20 litre recipe with a target original gravity, bitterness and colour.
The book holds 103 crosswords with answers

Beer Crosswords has 103 puzzles. The first 50 cover brewing in five parts, from malt, hops, yeast and water to lagers, Belgian beers and stouts. Part six is a course companion with one puzzle for each lesson of our courses, 53 in all. Four of those follow the four Brewing Fundamentals modules.

The clues come straight from the syllabus. "Mashing at 62 to 65 °C (144 to 149 °F) makes the beer this" is a clue for DRIER. "First brewhouse stop: crack the grain" is MILL. Answers sit at the back of the book, so you can check yourself without a tutor.
Words you have to recall stay longer than words you only read

A slide that says "mash pH should sit at 5.2 to 5.6" is easy to nod at and easy to forget. A clue that asks for the term that should sit at 5.2 to 5.6 makes you dig the answer out yourself. That small effort is what helps it stay.

That is the job the book does after each session. Fifteen minutes on the puzzle for that module turns the day's vocabulary into words you can use on brew day. It also works well for revision before you move on to a first recipe at home, which our guide to calculating ABV will help with.
Learning in a room changes what you notice

Some things are hard to teach through a screen. One of them is the hydrometer. Most read true at 20 °C (68 °F), so a sample read hot gives a low number and a wrong ABV. In a room we put the jar in your hand, take a reading hot, cool the sample and read it again, so you see the error yourself.

The same goes for smelling a crushed malt next to a whole one or feeling how sticky a sanitised surface is not. These are small moments. They are the reason this bundle is taught in person.

Sanitation is the other lesson that lands better in person. A no-rinse sanitiser needs the right dilution and contact time to work. A fermenter that looks clean can still carry a film of soil that sanitiser cannot get through. Cleaning comes first and sanitising second. Seeing a brewer do both in order, then doing it yourself, is how the habit forms before your first batch at home.
Who the bundle suits and how to book

It suits beer lovers ready to brew a first real recipe, homebrewers who want to know why a batch worked and hospitality staff who talk about beer every day. No science background is needed. If brewing might become a career, read our guide to becoming a brewer in India next.

Dates and venues in each of the four cities are confirmed on enquiry. Your first step is the enquiry form: choose Brewing Fundamentals, name your city and say you want the ₹1,999 bundle with the book.
